message.content: {"rules":["An Allocator implementation must handle zero-sized allocations even if its underlying allocator does not support them or returns a null pointer for them; the implementation must catch those cases.","A memory block whose starting address was returned by an allocator's allocate, grow, or shrink method must point to valid memory until the block is deallocated or the allocator is dropped. A call to deallocate or a successful grow or shrink deallocates the block; a grow or shrink returning Err does not.","Copying, cloning, or moving an allocator must not invalidate memory blocks returned from it.","A copied or cloned allocator must behave like the original allocator.","A currently allocated memory block may be passed to any method of its allocator that accepts such an argument. Here, currently allocated means its starting address was previously returned by that allocator's allocate, grow, or shrink method and it has not subsequently been deallocated by deallocate or a successful grow or shrink; grow or shrink returning Err does not deallocate it."]}
